11.4 Exercises 11- Exercises on abelian groups (S) Notation: if 𝐺 has a subgroup that is isomorphic to a group 𝐻, then we write 𝐻 ≲ 𝐺. Question 11.4.1. Let 𝐺 and 𝐻 be groups. Prove that 𝐺 × 𝐻 ≅ 𝐻 × 𝐺. Question 11.4.2. Let 𝐺 and 𝐻 be groups, with 𝐾 ≤ 𝐺 and 𝐽 ≤ 𝐻. Prove that 𝐾 × 𝐽 ≤ 𝐺 × 𝐻. Question 11.4.3. Let 𝑝 be a prime and let 𝑟, 𝑠 ≥ 0 be integers. Prove that if 𝑠 ≤ 𝑟, then 𝐶𝑝𝑠 ≲ 𝐶𝑝𝑟 (i.e. the group 𝐶𝑝𝑟 has a subgroup that is isomorphic to 𝐶𝑝𝑠). Question 11.4.4. Find, up to isomorphism, all abelian groups of order 72. Question 11.4.5. Is the following true? Give a proof or counterexample. If 𝐺 is a finite abelian group of order 𝑚, and 𝑘∣𝑚, then 𝐺 has a subgroup of order 𝑘.

Hint. (Question 0.1.1) Try the map 𝜃 ∶ 𝐺 × 𝐻 → 𝐻 × 𝐺 given by 𝜃((𝑔, ℎ)) = (ℎ, 𝑔). Hint. (Question 0.1.2) Use the quick subgroup test. Hint. (Question 0.1.3) Try to find an element ℎ ∈ 𝐶𝑝𝑟 that has order 𝑝𝑠. Then 𝐻 = ⟨ℎ⟩ ≅ 𝐶𝑝𝑠. Hint. (Question 0.1.4) Use the Fundamental Theorem of Finite Abelian Groups. Hint. (Question 0.1.5) This is a tricky question! Use The Fundamental Theorem of Finite Abelian Groups and the statements in Questions 0.1.2 and 0.1.3.
